head: HEAD
description:
Review the bundled demo shop's user-visible cart and checkout behavior. Exercise adding
a widget and completing an ordinary purchase. Also examine the expired-card path, which
the repository describes as a known defect, while distinguishing an expected payment
rejection from an unrelated application or browser failure.

journeys.title: Shopper adds a widget to the cart via the shop UI
journeys.persona: First-time shopper browsing the demo shop
journeys.goal: Add a widget to a new cart and see it reflected in the cart view with the correct price
journeys.because: ui.py exposes a form on GET /ui that posts to /ui/cart/items, and the shop must show the added item and its price in the resulting cart page

state: Shop has been reset so no prior cart exists

steps.do: Navigate to /ui in a fresh unauthenticated browser
steps.see: The shop page loads showing a product selection form with a dropdown of catalog SKUs (including widget) and a quantity field

steps.do: Select 'widget' from the product dropdown, leave quantity at 1, and submit the form
steps.see: The browser is taken to a cart page listing the widget with its unit price shown

steps.do: Observe the cart total on the resulting cart page
steps.see: The cart total equals the widget's listed unit price (price shown in the earlier dropdown, e.g. 1000 cents) for quantity 1

journeys.title: Shopper completes an ordinary purchase with a valid card
journeys.goal: Add an item to the cart and check out successfully with a valid card, receiving order confirmation
journeys.because: ui.py's /ui/checkout route confirms an order and clears the cart for any card_token that is not 'declined' or 'expired' (i.e. 'valid')

state: Shop has been reset so no prior cart exists

steps.do: Navigate to /ui in a fresh unauthenticated browser
steps.see: The shop page loads with the product selection form

steps.do: Select 'gadget' from the product dropdown, set quantity to 2, and submit the form
steps.see: The cart page shows the gadget line item with quantity 2 and a computed total

steps.do: On the cart page, submit checkout using the valid card token
steps.see: The browser is taken to an order confirmation page showing 'Order confirmed' and a non-empty order reference

steps.do: Navigate back to the same cart URL after confirmation
steps.see: The cart is now empty, consistent with the order having been placed and the cart cleared

journeys.title: Shopper's card is declined and the cart is preserved for retry
journeys.persona: Shopper whose card is rejected by the payment processor
journeys.goal: Attempt checkout with a declined card and confirm the shop reports the decline while keeping the cart items intact
journeys.because: Both ui.py and app.py document that a 'declined' card token must show a decline message while preserving the cart so the shopper can retry with another card

state: Cart contains at least one item

steps.do: Navigate to /ui and add a widget to a new cart
steps.see: The cart page shows the widget item and a total

steps.do: Submit checkout on the cart page using the 'declined' card token
steps.see: The page shows an alert stating 'Card was declined.'

steps.do: Inspect the cart contents shown on that same declined-checkout response
steps.see: The cart still lists the previously added widget item with its price, unchanged from before the attempt

journeys.title: Shopper's card is expired and the shop's handling is checked against intended behavior
journeys.persona: Shopper whose stored card has expired
journeys.goal: Attempt checkout with an expired card and verify the rejection message correctly names the card as expired and that the cart remains available for retry, as a decline would
journeys.because: The repository documents a deliberate defect: the expired-card path shows a generic 'Payment failed.' message that never names the card as expired, and it clears the cart unlike the declined path; the correct/intended behavior (matching the declined-card precedent and the human-confirmed expectation) is that the message should name the expiration and the cart should survive for retry

state: Cart contains at least one item

steps.do: Navigate to /ui and add 3 widgets to a new cart
steps.see: The cart page shows the widget line item with quantity 3 and a total

steps.do: Submit checkout on the cart page using the 'expired' card token
steps.see: The payment is rejected and the failure message explains the card is expired (naming expiration explicitly), not a generic 'Payment failed.' message

steps.do: Inspect the cart contents shown after the expired-card rejection
steps.see: The cart still contains the 3 widgets so the shopper can retry with a different card, rather than being cleared

journeys.title: Shopper attempts to check out a cart that no longer exists
journeys.persona: Shopper returning to a stale or invalid cart link
journeys.goal: Confirm that submitting checkout for a cart id the server does not recognize is rejected with a clear not-found message rather than a crash
journeys.because: ui.py's /ui/checkout handler explicitly checks 'if cart_id not in state.carts' and returns a 'We could not find that cart.' alert

state: Shop has been reset (so no carts exist yet)

steps.do: Navigate directly to /ui/cart/does-not-exist in a fresh unauthenticated browser (simulating a stale bookmarked cart link)
steps.see: The cart page for that id renders without items, consistent with an unknown/empty cart view rather than a server crash

steps.do: From that page, attempt to submit a checkout form pointed at the same nonexistent cart id with the valid card token
steps.see: The page shows an alert stating the cart could not be found, and no order confirmation is produced

unresolved: No README, Makefile, Dockerfile, or explicit launch script was present in the reviewed evidence, so the concrete command to start the demo app as a standalone browser-reachable server (module path, host, port) could not be determined; server.py only shows an in-process ephemeral-port harness (`serve()`) intended for test usage, not a documented standalone CLI invocation.

No dedicated browser-navigable health-check URL was documented; app.py exposes GET /health as a JSON API endpoint (L92-L94) but no UI page was shown confirming readiness, so health_url could not be confirmed with evidence.
The full set of valid CARD_TOKENS values beyond 'valid', 'declined', and 'expired' was not shown (import site only, no definition body), so it is unresolved whether other token behaviors exist.
No environment variables or secrets were referenced anywhere in the reviewed evidence, so required_env could not be populated; confirm whether any exist.

The exact reset mechanism reachable from the browser (vs. the POST /reset API used by the pytest fixture) was not shown as a UI-navigable action; unresolved whether journeys can rely on a UI-level reset or must depend on the API reset before each journey.

sources.ui.py#L81-L94: GET /ui shop page form with product dropdown and quantity input, used for add-to-cart journey entry point
sources.ui.py#L96-L120: POST /ui/cart/items and GET /ui/cart/{cart_id} routes confirming cart view rendering after adding items
sources.ui.py#L120-L155: POST /ui/checkout handler showing unknown-cart, declined, expired (deliberate defect), and successful order confirmation branches
sources.app.py#L96-L115: POST /cart/items API behavior for unknown SKU and cart creation, cross-referenced for intended add-to-cart semantics
sources.app.py#L117-L121: GET /cart/{cart_id} API behavior for unknown cart, used to corroborate 'unknown cart' UI behavior
sources.app.py#L123-L154: POST /checkout/submit API showing declined and expired card branches, including the documented deliberate defect in the expired-card message and cart-clearing behavior
sources.server.py#L1-L51: In-process ephemeral-port server harness noted as used for real-origin browser testing; no standalone CLI command documented
sources.e2e/test_shop_flows.py#L1-L70: Hand-written end-to-end tests describing intended shopper flows: add item, valid checkout, expired-card preserving cart, unknown SKU rejection
